pages.title: WXSAT
pages.text: Weather pictures from a $(l:radiocraft:repeaters/satellites)commercial satellite$() in $(thing)IMAGING$() mode: it scans the ground and sends the picture down line by line, as NOAA's APT satellites do.

pages.title: The station
pages.text: Install WXSAT and link a radio to the computer (touching it, on its data wire, or beside its scanner), tuned to the satellite's downlink. A VHF receiver channel or a commercial radio will do; with Doppler on, retune as it passes.$(br2)WXSAT is a background service: the computer stays on and records every pass with nobody at the screen. It draws power while it is installed. SETUP's 197609thing)Services197609) page can turn that off: then WXSAT records only while it is open on the screen.

pages.title: What you see
pages.text: Radar over the ground, in map colours: seas blue, land in its biome's colours, rain from light green through yellow and red, magenta in a severe storm's core and purple for hail, blues for snow.$(br2)A strong signal gives clean lines. Low in the sky the lines get snowy, and near the noise some go missing, as real APT does. About 8 blocks a pixel, 2,048 blocks wide.

pages.title: Live, mosaic, loop
pages.text: $(li)$(thing)F5$(): the live strip, filling in as the pass comes in, with the signal and the next imaging passes.$(li)$(thing)F6$(): the mosaic. Passes are stitched onto the map round the station, newest on top. Arrows pan, $(thing)F8$() zooms, Home comes back.$(li)$(thing)F7$(): the loop, pass by pass, to watch storms move. Space pauses, PgUp/PgDn step.

pages.title: Saving and printing
pages.text: $(thing)F3$() saves the view as a 128 by 128 .IMG. $(thing)F4$() prints it on the $(l:radiocraft:computer/scanner)scanner$(): an empty map or photo paper takes the picture; plain paper takes the area, the pass and its time, and how much rain or snow it shows.$(br2)The computer keeps the last eight passes, a few days at most, within about 3,500 blocks. Show them on an $(l:radiocraft:computer/external_crt_monitor)External CRT Monitor$().
A blank floppy and a lightning rod.
